# Text Annotations {#ggplot2-text-annotations}

## How text annotations work in ggplot2 {#introduction}

:::{.callout-note}
## Why this matters

Direct labels and annotations point at the story instead of making readers scan a legend.
:::

:::{.callout-warning}
## Common pitfall

Over-annotating every point creates clutter; annotate only the points that change the conclusion.
:::

In this chapter, we will learn to add text to plots.

- add custom text 
- modify color
- modify size
- modify fontface
- modify angle

## How to annotate plots with text in ggplot2 {#annotate}

We will use the `annotate()` function to add custom text to plots. You can 
also use the `annotate()` function to add rectangles, segments or pointranges,
but our focus will be on text. Let us start with a simple scatter plot.

```{r ann1, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
```

`annotate()` takes the following arguments:

- `geom`     : specify text
- `x`        : x axis location
- `y`        : y axis location
- `label`    : custom text 
- `color`    : color of text
- `size`     : size of text
- `fontface` : fontface of text
- `angle`    : angle of text

### How to add text labels to a ggplot2 plot {#add-text}

Let us begin by adding text to a scatter plot. We will use the mtcars data set
and examine the relationship between displacement and miles per gallon. To add
the text, we indicate that we are using `annotate()` for text, and we do this
by making the first input the word `'text'`. Now, ggplot2 knows that it should
add text to the plot but it still needs other information such as:

- where the text should appear on the plot, i.e. the location of the text
- and the text itself

We will provide the location by specifying points on the X and Y axis. These
are also the second and third inputs to `annotate()`, and the final input is
the text itself, which in our example is `'Sample Text'`.

```{r ann2, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  annotate('text', x = 200, y = 30, label = 'Sample Text')
```

### How to change text annotation color in ggplot2 {#color}

Now that we know how to add text, let us look at modifying its appearance. To
change the color, use the `color` argument. In the example below, we modify the
color to `'red'`.

```{r ann4, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  annotate('text', x = 200, y = 30, label = 'Sample Text', color = 'red')
```

### How to change text annotation size in ggplot2 {#size}

Use the `size` argument to modify the size of the text.

```{r ann5, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  annotate('text', x = 200, y = 30, label = 'Sample Text', size = 6)
```

### How to change text annotation font face in ggplot2 {#font}

To change the font face (for example, `'bold'` or `'italic'`), use the
`fontface` argument.

```{r ann6, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  annotate('text', x = 200, y = 30, label = 'Sample Text', fontface = 'bold')
```

### How to rotate text annotations in ggplot2 {#angle}

Use the `angle` argument to modify the angle of the text. In the example below,
we modify the angle of the text to `25`.

```{r ann7, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  annotate('text', x = 200, y = 30, label = 'Sample Text', angle = 25)
```

## How to combine text annotation options in ggplot2 {#putting-it-all-together}

```{r ann3, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  annotate('text', x = 200, y = 30, label = 'Sample Text',
           color = 'red', size = 6, fontface = 'bold', angle = 25)
```

## Exercises

1. Annotate the highest-mpg car with `annotate("text", ...)`.
2. Label only cars with `mpg > 30` using `geom_text()`.
3. Decide which two points deserve labels and justify the restraint.
